slides.title: Requirement-Driven Design of Whole-Body Social Tactile Sensing via Virtual Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: This work proposes a framework to derive whole-body tactile sensing requirements from VR-based interaction data, supporting the development of embodied social robots for RwB.

card.one_liner: A requirement-driven framework using VR to determine optimal tactile sensor placement and resolution for social robots.
card.key_idea: VR-based interaction data is collected to reconstruct contact geometry, allowing researchers to simulate and optimize sensor coverage and spatial resolution before physical hardware fabrication.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via a 5,520-trial dataset with 18 participants using Random Forest and CNN-GRU classifiers; leave-one-subject-out cross-validation was used.
card.limitation: Simulations use binary contact signals (no force/pressure) and were conducted only on a single robot's arm in VR.

slides.title: Representation-Aligned Tactile Grounding for Contact-Rich Robotic Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a Latent Tactile Predictor that aligns intermediate action representations with future contact outcomes to improve contact-rich manipulation.

card.one_liner: Improves contact-rich robotic manipulation by aligning future tactile prediction with intermediate action-expert representations.
card.key_idea: Uses linear probes to identify an intermediate representation for a Latent Tactile Predictor (LTP), which supervises action-conditioned contact dynamics via compact latent embeddings.
card.evaluation: Tested on five real-world tasks using SmolVLA and π0 backbones; achieved 74% and 73% average success, outperforming VLM-side and final-state grounding.

slides.title: Never Too Late for Force: Accelerating VLA Post-Training with Reactive Force Injection
slides.highlight: LIFT introduces a framework for adding contact reactivity to VLA policies using 6D end-effector force, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on physics/force-based skill acquisition.

card.one_liner: LIFT accelerates VLA post-training by injecting reactive force feedback to improve contact-rich manipulation performance.
card.key_idea: Grafts a reactive action expert with causal force memory and zero-initialized cross-attention onto a pretrained VLA, trained via online DAgger.
card.evaluation: Tested on towel folding, book insertion, and Hanoi ring placement; LIFT outperformed vision-only DAgger and single-frame force baselines.
card.limitation: Relies on human corrections during online DAgger, limiting data throughput, and was only evaluated on single-arm manipulation.

slides.title: Towards Artificial Nerves: Biomimetic Optical-Fiber Tactile Sensing for Robots
slides.highlight: OptiTac introduces a biomimetic tactile sensor using optical fibers as artificial nerves to achieve high spatial resolution and interpretable contact sensing.

card.one_liner: OptiTac is a biomimetic tactile sensor using optical fibers to transmit high-resolution touch data to remote cameras.
card.key_idea: A one-to-one pairing of mechanical pins and optical fibers mimics human nerves, enabling interpretable contact inference via analytical image moments instead of deep learning.
card.evaluation: Tested with various indenters for localization, size, and shape; achieved sub-millimeter RMSE and 96% shape classification accuracy using GMM and Hu moments.
card.limitation: Performance was demonstrated under controlled laboratory conditions with short fibers; robustness to long routing, bending, and environmental variation is not yet quantified.

slides.title: VTAP Gripper: Synergizing Fingertip Sensing and a Visuo-Tactile Active Palm for Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a gripper combining a visuo-tactile active palm with tactile array sensors to achieve robust grasping and fine manipulation. It utilizes a gesture-conditioned retargeting framework for teleoperation, enabling complex tasks like syringe reorientation and peg-in-hole insertion.

card.one_liner: A 13-DOF gripper combining an active visuo-tactile palm and tactile fingertips for dexterous in-hand manipulation.
card.key_idea: Integrates a bi-modal palm (switching between vision and tactile sensing) with compliant fingers and a gesture-conditioned retargeting framework for human-to-robot teleoperation.
card.evaluation: Tested on YCB objects, syringes, and peg-in-hole tasks. Achieved 93.3% grasping success and 65-70% success in complex manipulation tasks.
card.limitation: VR hand-tracking occlusions can cause unintentional grasp release during teleoperation, particularly when the headset is close to the hand.

slides.title: MIDAS Hand: Modular low-Impedance Direct-drive Anthropomorphic Sensing Hand
slides.highlight: The MIDAS Hand provides a human-scale platform with integrated tactile sensing and low backdrive torque, supporting the human-to-robot data collection and physics-based sensing required for MOSAIC.

card.one_liner: An open-source, human-scale dexterous hand featuring low-impedance direct-drive actuation and dense tactile sensing.
card.key_idea: A 3D-printed, modular hand with 13 active DoFs, using rigid linkages for backdrivability and integrating 283 three-axis tactile taxels for contact-rich manipulation.
card.evaluation: Validated via GRASP taxonomy (32/33 types), backdrive torque measurements (~0.02 Nm), payload tests (>9.5kg), and 5,000+ cycle reliability tests.
card.limitation: Lacks a little finger, limiting ulnar-side support, and tactile sensing is not yet integrated into closed-loop control.

slides.title: Catch, Throw, Repeat: Planning for Human-Robot Partner Juggling
slides.highlight: This work presents a planning and control architecture for synchronized multi-ball juggling between humans and robots, contributing to the study of physical human-robot interaction relevant to RwB.

card.one_liner: A real-time planning system enabling a robot to perform synchronized multi-ball partner juggling with humans.
card.key_idea: Integrates predictive ball tracking (Kalman filters), adaptive online trajectory optimization via multiple-shooting, and state-machine-based coordination logic to manage catch-and-throw decisions.
card.evaluation: User study with 8 participants; achieved 3-ball cascades and 100% success in 1-ball settings. Results exceed previous records; validated via MuJoCo simulations.
card.limitation: Performance is constrained by timing pressure at high ball counts and a lack of explicit inter-ball collision avoidance.

slides.title: Scalable Open-Source Visuotactile Sensor for 6-Axis Contact Wrench Estimation in Tensegrity Robots
slides.tldr: OPEN-SOURCE VISUOTACTILE SENSOR FOR TENSEGRITY ROBOTS
slides.highlight: This work introduces a scalable visuotactile sensor using a neural network to estimate six-axis contact wrenches, enhancing state estimation and contact detection for tensegrity robots.

card.one_liner: An open-source visuotactile sensor for tensegrity robots enabling 6-axis contact wrench estimation and ground detection.
card.key_idea: Combines a fisheye camera and LED ring with a 3D-printed TPU interface and elastomer shell, using a residual MLP to map shear vector fields to wrenches.
card.evaluation: Validated via KUKA robot and ATI F/T sensor (MSE 0.1531 static); tested on a 12kg tensegrity robot for binary contact detection.
card.limitation: Torque estimation is less accurate than force due to camera latency, processing lag, and lack of temporal modeling.
